summary:
Lunar Outpost Alpha is an interactive space survival game that runs right in your web browser. You play as Mission Control, communicating with an AI astronaut named Alex Rivera who is stationed alone on the Moon for 13 days.

Using a constant stream of station updates, the game challenges you to keep Alex alive as new emergencies strike every day—like oxygen leaks, dust-covered solar panels, and power failures. Rather than acting like a basic chatbot, Alex tracks his own hunger, energy, and safety, refusing to rest if a dangerous problem still needs fixing.

It matters because it turns standard AI into an engaging, live problem-solving experience and it teaches real life scenarios effectively sure.
details:
Lunar Outpost Alpha is a browser-based game where you act as Mission Control helping an astronaut named Alex survive a 13-day mission on the Moon.

  • how it works: You type instructions into a retro computer terminal to help Alex fix daily problems: like clearing moon dust off solar panels or patching air leaks; while keeping an eye on his health, energy, and life support systems.
  • Benefits: It runs fast and smoothly in any web browser without needing heavy software downloads or complicated setups.
  • Intended impact: It makes learning about space exploration and problem-solving fun and engaging through an interactive storytelling experience.
  • Tools, languages, and software: It was built using simple web coding languages (HTML and JavaScript), styled with clean design tools (Tailwind CSS), powered by smart AI technology for the astronaut's responses, and hosted online via Vercel.
  • Creativity: Instead of a boring chatbot, it turns talking with an AI into an immersive survival game complete with blinking terminal screens, ticking clocks, and emergency alerts.
  • Factors considered: The team focused on keeping the design simple and reliable so that anyone can easily play it on a computer or phone without technical glitches
dataRefs: NASA Solar Storms and Flares Portal.
